root.label: Hazard pointers and RCU
root.note: C++26 safe reclamation: writers retire objects and the library deletes them once no reader can still use them.

children.label: The reclamation problem
children.note: A lock-free reader may still dereference an object that a writer has just unlinked.

children.label: Retire, not delete
children.note: Writers hand removed objects to the library, which picks a safe moment to call the deleter.

children.label: Status
children.note: P2530R3 and P2545R4, adopted June 2023; feature-test macros are 202306L.

children.label: Implementations
children.note: Neither libstdc++ 16 nor libc++ 21 ships the headers; Folly is the reference implementation.

children.label: Hazard pointers
children.note: A reader publishes the address it uses; reclamation skips retired objects whose address is published.

children.label: hazard_pointer_obj_base
children.note: Exactly one public non-virtual base of this type makes T hazard-protectable and stores its deleter.

children.label: make_hazard_pointer
children.note: Constructs an owned, unassociated hazard pointer; may throw bad_alloc.

children.label: Empty object
children.note: Default-constructed or moved-from; protect and reset_protection on it are undefined behavior.

children.label: try_protect
children.note: Publish, reload src with acquire, clear protection if it changed; returns whether it was stable.

children.label: swap
children.note: Exchanges ownership without ending or starting any protection epoch.

children.label: Retirement rules
children.note: What retire requires and what it does.

children.label: At most once
children.note: Retiring the same object twice is undefined behavior.

children.label: Deleter must not throw
children.note: Undefined behavior if reclaiming or a scheduled evaluation exits via an exception.

children.label: Intrusive retire is noexcept
children.note: The deleter lives in the base class, so the member retire never allocates.

children.label: rcu_retire may throw
children.note: The non-intrusive form may allocate, throwing bad_alloc; on throw nothing is scheduled.

children.label: RCU
children.note: Readers bracket work in regions; deleters run only after every region that could have seen the object ends.

children.label: rcu_domain is Lockable
children.note: Meets Cpp17Lockable, so use std::scoped_lock on rcu_default_domain().

children.label: try_lock always true
children.note: Equivalent to lock(); readers never wait for writers.

children.label: Nested regions
children.note: unlock closes the most recently opened region on that domain in the same thread.

children.label: No reader retries
children.note: A reader sees either the old or the new version and never has to start over.

children.label: Waiting
children.note: Two blocking calls with different jobs; neither implies the other.

children.label: rcu_synchronize
children.note: Blocks until every pre-existing region on the domain has ended; does not run deleters.

children.label: rcu_barrier
children.note: Blocks until every deleter scheduled before the call has been evaluated.

children.label: Self-deadlock
children.note: rcu_synchronize inside your own region waits for an unlock that comes after it, so it never returns.

children.label: No hazard cleanup
children.note: C++26 has no call that forces hazard-pointer reclamation, and no custom domains.

children.label: Choosing
children.note: Hazard pointers replace reference counts; RCU replaces reader-writer locks.

children.label: Bounded garbage
children.note: Hazard pointers bound possibly-reclaimable objects; one stalled RCU reader holds back all deletion.

children.label: Reader cost
children.note: RCU reads are almost free; hazard pointers cost a publish and reload per protected object.

children.label: Writers still synchronize
children.note: Both make deletion safe only; concurrent writers need a mutex or compare-and-swap.
